slot.brief: Four reagents listed for a given substrate transformation — three accomplish it, one does not; identify the odd one out.

stem: Which of the following 1-halopropanes reacts slowest with NaI in dry acetone via an SN2 mechanism?

verdicts.working: For SN2 reactions of primary alkyl halides, the rate increases with leaving-group ability: I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻. Thus 1-fluoropropane reacts slowest.

working:
In SN2 reactions, the rate depends on the leaving group ability. Good leaving groups are weak bases. Leaving group ability order: I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻. Fluoride is the poorest leaving group due to strong C–F bond and high basicity. Hence 1-fluoropropane undergoes SN2 slowest.

Independent check: For SN2 reactions of primary alkyl halides, the rate increases with leaving-group ability: I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻. Thus 1-fluoropropane reacts slowest.
solution: In an $S_N2$ reaction, rate increases with leaving-group ability: $I^- > Br^- > Cl^- > F^-$. The C–F bond is strong, making $F^-$ the poorest leaving group; hence 1-fluoropropane reacts slowest.
